### Contributing guidelines

- [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
- [x] I have updated 'mini.nvim' to latest version of the `main` branch

### Module(s)

mini.icons

### Neovim version

0.11.x

### Description

Thanks @echasnovski, for your response in the previous [issue](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/issues/1892). But proposed solution doesn't work, because the the `file` argument returns the base-name of the file, not the full path. But I did find an alternative solution, and am just pointing out your mistake.

Proposed solution:

```Lua
local hyprland_conf_basenames = {
    ["animations.conf"] = true,
    ["hypridle.conf"] = true,
    ["hyprland.conf"] = true,
    ["hyprlock.conf"] = true,
    -- etc.
}

return {
    "echasnovski/mini.icons",
    config = function()
        require("mini.icons").setup {
            use_file_extension = function(ext, file)
                -- If the file doesn't have a ".conf" extension,
                -- we check its extension icon (return true).
                if ext ~= "conf" then
                    return true
                end

                -- If the file's basename is one of the Hyprland configs,
                -- return false to tell 'mini.icons' NOT to use the "conf" extension icon.
                -- This allows the default "hyprlang" filetype icon to be used.
                if hyprland_conf_basenames[file] then
                    return false
                end

                -- If it's a ".conf" file but NOT a Hyprland config,
                -- return true to USE the "conf" extension icon explicitly defined.
                return true
            end,
            -- other code
            extension = {
                -- other code
                conf = { glyph = "", hl = "SettingsIconColor" },
                -- other code
            },
            -- other code
        MiniIcons.mock_nvim_web_devicons()
    end,
}


```

### Reproduction

Steps to reproduce:

1. Ensure you have `mini.icons` installed and configured in your Neovim setup.
2. Place the `use_file_extension` code block previously suggested by the maintainer into your `mini.icons` configuration.

```Lua
require('mini.icons').setup({
  use_file_extension = function(ext, file)
    print(ext)
    print(file)
    if ext ~= 'conf' then return true end
    -- Use icon from extension only if it is not for Hyprland config
    return file:find('/hypr/[^/]+%.conf$') == nil
  end,
  extension = {
    conf = { glyph = '', hl = 'SettingsIconColor' },
    -- other settings
  },
  -- other settings
})
```
(I added the `print()` lines)

4. Exit Neovim.
5. Open a Hyprland config file with Neovim, run the `:messages` command, and observe the results.
title: The `file` argument in `use_file_extension` is a basename, not the full path
